model_answer:
**Amazon (AMZN) — roughly $125 billion.**

Based on the most recent (Q3 2025) guidance each company has given for full-year 2025 capex:

| Company | 2025 capex guidance | Latest update |
|---|---|---|
| **Amazon** | **~$125B** | Raised from ~$118B on the Oct 30, 2025 Q3 call |
| **Alphabet (GOOG/GOOGL)** | **$91–93B** | Raised from ~$85B on the Oct 29, 2025 Q3 call |
| **Meta** | **$70–72B** | Narrowed/raised from $66–72B on the Oct 29, 2025 Q3 call |

Details:
- **Amazon:** CFO Brian Olsavsky said Amazon expects full-year cash capex of ~$125B in 2025 (up ~50% YoY), with the amount increasing again in 2026. Q3 capex alone was $34.2B; nine-month spend was ~$120B. Most goes to AWS AI infrastructure (including Trainium chips) plus fulfillment/robotics.
- **Alphabet:** CFO Anat Ashkenazi guided to $91–93B for 2025, noting ~60% of technical infrastructure spend is servers and 40% data centers/networking, and promising a "significant increase" in 2026.
- **Meta:** CFO Susan Li guided to $70–72B for 2025 (including finance-lease principal payments) and said capex *dollar growth* will be "notably larger" in 2026 as compute needs expanded beyond prior expectations.

So Amazon is the biggest spender in absolute dollars — about $32–35B more than Alphabet and roughly $53–55B more than Meta. (Note: Amazon's figure is a "cash capex" number; including finance leases it would be slightly higher still, so the ranking is unchanged.)

Sources: [Amazon Q3 2025 earnings release/8-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1018724/000101872425000121/amzn-20250930xex991.htm); [Alphabet Q3 2025 earnings call](https://abc.xyz/investor/events/event-details/2025/2025-q3-earnings-call-2025-4oi4bac_q9/default.aspx); [Meta Q3 2025 earnings call transcript](https://exa.ai/library/markets/stocks/META/earnings/FY2025/Q3/transcript).
judge_reason: Conclusion that Amazon spends the most is correct, but the stated capex figures are later revised values that do not match the official rubric amounts and trigger contradiction.
